sentences.text:
By way of this petition, petitioner has put to challenge the order passed by the disciplinary authority Annexure P-5 dated 23.01.2024, whereby the penalty of discharge from service has been imposed on the petitioner, which has been further confirmed in appeal vide order Annexure P-7, dated 10.06.2024.
2.

The facts of the case for the purpose of disposal of present petition are that the petitioner was posted as Constable in M.P. Special Armed Force (SAF), which was initially under Section 363 against unnamed persons, but after recovery of the girl, offence under Sections 363, 366, 376, 120-B and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act was registered.

The main offence of taking away the girl and committing the act of sexual assault against her was registered against the nephew of the petitioner,
namely Dheeru Bagadi and the father of main accused, his brother and petitioner being uncle of main accused were roped in on the allegation that the petitioner was one of the persons who threatened the victim to go with the main accused.

The victim was recovered after many months when she had resided NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56310 2 WP-26105-2024 with the main accused at various places including Palwal (Haryana), Gujarat, etc.

The victim turned hostile before the trial Court, but looking to the position that she was around 15 years of age,
therefore, the main accused Dheeru Bagadhi was convicted, but other accused persons were acquitted.

3. The trial against the other accused persons, i.e. the main accused Dheeru Bagadhi, his father and brother was concluded vide judgment dated 17.05.2019 and when the knowledge of the said judgment reached the respondent authorities, then they came to know that the petitioner has been declared absconder in the said case and trial against the petitioner has not been conducted.

sentences.text: preliminary enquiry was carried out against the petitioner and its report is Annexure P-4, which indicates that the information of petitioner being absconder in the said case reached the authorities in the year 2019 itself and a preliminary enquiry was carried out.

4. The petitioner was questioned in the preliminary enquiry that why he is absconding in the criminal case, to which he replied that since he is living since long with his in-laws at district Panna and he is not in touch with his brother and his family, therefore, he has no knowledge that he is wanted in any criminal case and even if he has been named then it is a case of false implication.

The said preliminary enquiry report dated 13.02.2020 was submitted to the disciplinary authority and the disciplinary authority then issued a charge sheet in the year 2023 vide Annexure P-3.
5.
In the intervening period, the petitioner had surrendered and was bailed out after one day and trial against him ensued only under section 120-B IPC and under no other provision.
After conducting the said trial, the Sessions Court recorded the judgment of acquittal dated 13.04.2024 against the petitioner.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56310 3 WP-26105-2024 6.

It is pertinent to mention here that the petitioner was not an accused in the said case under the main provision, but was an accused only under Section 120-B I.P.C. and the only allegation against him as per prosecution version was of threatening the victim along with the main accused and his brother etc. to go along with the main accused.
The victim turned hostile before the trial Court and apart from the main accused, who is stated to have committed sexual assault on the victim, all other accused persons have been acquitted.

7. It is really surprising that despite coming to know in the year 2019 that the petitioner has been declared absconder in a criminal case, the SAF did nothing in the matter and even issued charge sheet only in the year 2023.
The petitioner was serving the SAF and he could have been easily apprehended.

The petitioner had appeared before the Court, surrendered and faced trial in the year 2023 and was even acquitted by the trial Court on 13.04.2024.
8.

The charge against the petitioner was only as under:-
"   . 204      ,   (. .)   . -102/15         23.05.2023                            
            -64           -02,
03  04  . .      1965   03 (01)      "
9.

The charge against the petitioner was only of registration of criminal case NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56310 4 WP-26105-2024 and of getting arrested on 23.05.2023 and tarnishing the image of police force.

sentences.text: A person does not control the manner in which a third person registers FIR against him and in the present case also the petitioner could not have prevented registration of FIR against him in some other district, i.e. Satna, which is around 300 km away from his place of posting i.e. Sagar.
The petitioner duly faced trial and was acquitted under section 120-B, which was the only provision under which he had been charged.
11. Learned counsel for the State had vehemently argued that the petitioner remained absconding also.
However, this was not the charge against the petitioner.

Even if it is to be considered as part and parcel of the charge against the petitioner, then also the petitioner was a Mmember of SAF and it was very easy to arrest him and he was performing his duties for all the time.

Even the SAF came to know about he being declared offender in the year 2019, but did not take any steps for asking the petitioner to surrender nor informed the concerned district police to arrest the petitioner.

He was performing his duties assigned to him at district Sagar and the charge sheet was issued only when he had surrendered before the Court and decided to face trial in which he was ultimaely acquitted.
12. In view of the above, the ultimate acquittal of the petitioner in the criminal case cannot be ignored and overlooked.

The order of the disciplinary authority alleging that by arrest the petitioner has tarnished the image of police cannot be given stamp of approval in view of the consequential acquittal of the petitioner in the criminal case by the Ist A.S.J., Nagod, District Satna in S.T. No.11 of 2023 vide order (under Section 232 Cr.P.C.) dated 13.04.2024 .
13.

Consequently, it is found that the charges against the petitioner are not NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56310 5 WP-26105-2024 made out and the impugned orders deserve to be set aside and petitioner is entitled to be reinstated in service.

However, in the facts of the case, the petitioner shall not be entitled to any back wages till date of this order, but shall be entitled to all other consequential benefits to ensure continuity of service and seniority.

14. Let the petitioner be allowed to rejoin duties forthwith.
15.
Petition is allowed.
